wound_authority: Pre-ERISA common law trust standard for pension administrators; LMRA § 302 (29 U.S.C. § 186(c)(5)) for multi-employer funds
jurisdiction: Federal and state (patchwork — varied by state)
in_force_period: From establishment of private pension plans in the United States (early 20th century) until September 2, 1974
superseded_by: Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA), Pub. L. 93-406, signed September 2, 1974; specifically § 404 (codified at 29 U.S.C. § 1104)
current_status: SUPERSEDED — no longer operative as the governing standard for pension plan administrators. The pre-ERISA framework survives only as background historical law; it has no operative effect after September 2, 1974.
primary_sources_pending: S. Rep. No. 93-127 (Senate Labor Committee Report on ERISA, 1973) — describes pre-ERISA inadequacies in detail
H.R. Rep. No. 93-1280 (House Education and Labor Committee Report on ERISA, 1974)
Congressional Record, 93rd Cong., 2d Sess. (1974) — floor debate on § 404 fiduciary standard
Harvard College v. Amory, 26 Mass. 446 (1830) — original common law prudent man rule
29 U.S.C. § 186(c)(5) — LMRA § 302 multi-employer fund provision (pre-ERISA text)
verification_status: PARTIAL — framework description drawn from standard ERISA legislative history sources. Verbatim text of pre-ERISA plan documents and state pension statutes pending primary-source fetch.
purpose_of_preservation: Defensive historical record — accurate citation of the legal wound that 29 U.S.C. § 1104 was enacted to address. Required to demonstrate the magnitude of the ERISA reform and the specific gap the prudent expert standard closed.
filed_by: Claude (assistant) under steward direction — Michael Hartmann
